H1_UNCONSTRAINED_DAMAGE_READJUSTMENT.title: Unconstrained Structural Discrete Damage Readjustment
H1_UNCONSTRAINED_DAMAGE_READJUSTMENT.mechanism: The discrete phase-field equation [K_dd + M_dd(H)] d = f(H) is solved as an unconstrained linear system at each iteration without variational inequality enforcement (d_{n+1} >= d_n) or active-set projection on nodal DOF 3. Although constitutive history H is strictly monotonic, global residual equilibrium forces local decreases in d when neighboring crack tip nodes surge in damage.
evidence_supporting: 100.000% of integration points strictly satisfy delta H >= 0.0 MPa (Gate G4 PASS with min delta H = 0.000000 MPa).
89.2% of all negative damage instances (1,610/1,805) occur in fully severed crack wake (d >= 0.95) where stress is zero and material is completely severed.
Process-zone violations (175 instances) occur immediately adjacent to elements experiencing severe dynamic damage surges (Delta d up to +0.339).
Inspection of f42_mixed_uel.for confirms zero inequality constraints, penalties, or projections are applied to nodal array U(1..4) in JTYPE 1.
evidence_contradicting_or_limiting: Unconstrained damage readjustment explains local negative delta d values, but does not by itself explain why the displacement increment dt collapsed to 1e-11s. A linear unconstrained Poisson solve is unconditionally stable and would converge in 1 iteration if uncoupled.
H1_UNCONSTRAINED_DAMAGE_READJUSTMENT.falsifiable_criterion: Applying an active-set projection (d_{n+1} = max(d_n, d_{trial})) or variational inequality solver strictly eliminates all 1,805 negative damage instances (yielding min Delta d >= 0.0) without altering constitutive history H.

H2_NONLINEAR_COUPLING_FAILURE.title: Block-Diagonal Picard Tangent & Displacement-Damage Coupling Divergence
H2_NONLINEAR_COUPLING_FAILURE.mechanism: In f42_mixed_uel.for, Layer 1 provides AMATRX for DOF 3 (K_dd) and Layer 2 provides AMATRX for DOFs 1,2 (K_uu). The off-diagonal coupling tangents dR_u/dd and dR_d/du are identically ZERO. This constitutes a block-diagonal Picard approximation inside Abaqus's Newton-Raphson solver. When damage rates surge near the hole, omitting off-diagonal terms causes Newton-Raphson to lose quadratic convergence and oscillate.
evidence_supporting: Solver message file shows classic non-convergent oscillation between displacement residual and damage correction: in Inc 205 Attempt 3, Iter 1 has force residual at Node 7317 DOF 2, Iter 2 has damage correction at Node 6972 DOF 3, and Iter 4 diverges with message 'SOLUTION APPEARS TO BE DIVERGING'.

Analysis of f42_mixed_uel.for confirms Layer 1 AMATRX is dimensioned 4x4 (only DOF 3) and Layer 2 AMATRX is dimensioned 8x8 (only DOFs 1,2), proving zero cross-coupling terms exist in the global stiffness matrix.
COMMON-block SV_H_TRIAL ratchets upward during intra-increment Newton iterations without resetting, amplifying the coupling lag between trial displacement and trial damage.
evidence_contradicting_or_limiting: Block-diagonal Picard coupling converged successfully for 254 increments (all of Step 1 and Incs 1-204 of Step 2). The coupling divergence is therefore triggered only when spatial gradients or structural compliance change rapidly.
H2_NONLINEAR_COUPLING_FAILURE.falsifiable_criterion: Monolithic evaluation with true cross-coupling tangents (dR_u/dd and dR_d/du) or staggered alternate minimization with converged sub-iterations eliminates the cutback divergence at Node 7317/6972 without requiring dt < 1e-10s.

H3_SECONDARY_FRONT_UNDERRESOLUTION.title: Spatial Mesh Underresolution in Intermediate Distal Ligament
H3_SECONDARY_FRONT_UNDERRESOLUTION.mechanism: In the adapted mesh, the primary notch-to-hole corridor achieves h_min = 0.000685 mm <= l0/10.9 (96.3% compliant with h <= l0/2). However, in the intermediate ligament between the hole boundary (x=0.75 mm) and the right boundary, element sizes transition from h ~ 0.004 mm to h ~ 0.008 mm (1.06x to 2.13x l0/2). When the crack tip approaches the hole, the stress concentration across this coarse ligament cannot be resolved smoothly, driving steep local gradients into single elements.
evidence_supporting: Node 8056 (previous cutback locus) is located at (0.7505, 0.6558) mm, exactly 0.0005 mm from the hole right flank, where surrounding element size is h_mean = 0.00483 mm (1.29x l0/2).
Node 7317 (largest residual force in Inc 205) is located at (0.7482, 0.6621) mm with surrounding element size h_mean = 0.00512 mm (1.37x l0/2).

In Pandey & Kumar (2025) Figure 25(b), the secondary crack initiation zone is continuously refined to h <= l0/2 across the entire ligament, whereas Method A unrefined distal ligament leaves elements larger than l0/2.
evidence_contradicting_or_limiting: Underresolution alone does not prevent convergence in non-softening elasticity. It acts as an error amplifier that steepens the Picard coupling lag and exacerbates Newton divergence.
H3_SECONDARY_FRONT_UNDERRESOLUTION.falsifiable_criterion: Refining the distal ligament corridor to h <= l0/2 = 0.00375 mm reduces the local force residual at Node 7317, smoothing the stress transfer across the hole boundary.

H4_TOPOLOGICAL_TRANSITION_SINGULARITY.title: Topological Boundary Transition and Stress Relaxation Singularity
H4_TOPOLOGICAL_TRANSITION_SINGULARITY.mechanism: As the primary crack tip breaches the free surface of the off-axis hole (intersecting Node 1422 and Elements 1578, 2978-2981), the physical topology of the specimen transforms from a simply connected plate with a hole to a plate with an open re-entrant boundary notch. The traction-free boundary conditions of the hole suddenly relax the primary ligament stress, shifting the compliance and forcing rapid redistribution of internal forces into the secondary ligament.
evidence_supporting: Terminal increment Inc 204 reached uy = 0.0076766 mm, at which point 5 physical elements directly breach the hole boundary (d >= 0.95 at hole flank).
Load-displacement curve exhibits an inflection at Inc 201-204 where reaction force drops from 244.4 N to 229.4 N (59.87% post-peak drop).
The divergence in Inc 205 occurs precisely at the boundary intersection nodes (Nodes 7317, 6972, 7685) within 0.01 mm of the hole surface.
evidence_contradicting_or_limiting: The topological breach is a physical fracture event, not an algorithmic defect. A robust formulation must be capable of traversing boundary intersections without numerical collapse.
H4_TOPOLOGICAL_TRANSITION_SINGULARITY.falsifiable_criterion: Topological transition occurs naturally under displacement control; once the crack breaches the hole, secondary initiation requires further displacement advancement (uy > 0.0080 mm) under stable solver equilibrium.

primary_conclusions: 1. DAMAGE IRREVERSIBILITY FAILURE (Gate G3): Driven entirely by Hypothesis H1 (Unconstrained Discrete Damage Readjustment). While material history H is 100% monotonic, solving [K_dd + M_dd(H)] d = f(H) without inequality projection permits Poisson-smoothing oscillations down to min Delta d = -1.064e-3 in severed wake (89.2%) and process zone (9.7%).

2. INCREMENT-SIZE COLLAPSE (Gate G2): Driven by the synergy of Hypothesis H4 (Physical Trigger: Hole Breach) and Hypothesis H2 (Algorithmic Driver: Block-Diagonal Picard Coupling). When the crack breaches the hole, rapid stress relaxation requires tight displacement-damage coupling; omitting cross-coupling tangents (dRu/dd = 0) destroys Newton convergence, pinning dt < 1e-11s.
3. SPATIAL AMPLIFICATION: Hypothesis H3 (Distal Underresolution h ~ 1.3-1.6x l0/2) amplifies the coupling error near Node 7317 and Node 8056.
4. ISOLATED dt_min REDUCTION IS EMPIRICALLY EXHAUSTED: Relaxing dt_min to 1e-11s yielded 3 increments but hit the same fundamental Picard divergence. Lowering dt_min further is mathematically futile.

recommended_smallest_defensible_interven.title: Dual-Mechanism Resolution Strategy for Case 2
recommended_smallest_defensible_interven.offline_path: Formalize the discrete phase-field failure diagnosis as a definitive thesis finding on the limitations of unprojected block-diagonal UEL implementations in Abaqus/Standard.

implementation_path_options.option: Option A: Method A Multi-Corridor Refinement (Geometry / Mesh Path)
implementation_path_options.description: Refine the secondary distal ligament in the base Method A mesh so that h <= l0/2 = 0.00375 mm is satisfied continuously from notch to hole and from hole to boundary (eliminating Hypothesis H3).
implementation_path_options.pros: Preserves frozen UEL f42_mixed_uel.for unchanged; operates entirely within Method A adaptive remeshing framework.
implementation_path_options.cons: Does not fix the unprojected damage formulation (H1) or block-diagonal coupling (H2).

implementation_path_options.option: Option B: Benchmark Priority Rebalancing (Master Objective F1737 Path)
implementation_path_options.description: Consolidate Case 2's diagnostic findings (Gate G1 bitwise parity, 59.9% post-peak drop, complete primary breach, and forensic failure diagnosis) as a complete thesis benchmark, and transition research focus to Case 1 (Mode-I crack propagation along full ligament) and Cases 4 & 5 (coupled forward fracture simulations).
implementation_path_options.pros: Zero UEL modification required; maximizes progress toward December 13 research freeze across all 5 benchmark geometries; honors the independent review finding that Case 2 is already the most thoroughly diagnosed benchmark.
implementation_path_options.cons: Leaves Case 2 secondary crack propagation as an identified thesis limitation.
